why: A retired definition that is only 'not claimed' reads as a missing prerequisite. Recording it as not-applicable-by-design, with its reason and its counter-examples, is what stops later rounds from chasing it again.

entries.what: per-domain human reader signs the acknowledgement himself; a lane may not read on the owner's behalf
entries.why_retired: it presupposes that reading cannot be delegated, which contradicts the blueprint's Native E2E closed loop and unattended-automation intent (L0.md:377 role not person; L0.md:1242 the verification unit can be mechanised; L0.md:1564 owner-ordered automation is permitted but separation and true negatives are not skipped)
entries.measured_history: 0/6 — nobody ever signed in that capacity; kept as a measurement, not as a compliance state
do_not: cite it as a gap in a status report

counterexamples.wrong_reading: a lane may not read for the owner, so Done requires the owner to read every clause
counterexamples.consequence: breaks the Native E2E closed loop and makes unattended delivery structurally impossible
counterexamples.correct: three independent lanes read, complement and correct each other; the owner authorises and accepts risk
